Now that's an interesting life. Let's ask something practical. I always wondered, how much time does it takes to go from average poker player who likes the game but don't know much, to pro player who can actually grind a decent amount of money every months ? Internet makes the game easier, since you can play a LOT of hands by hour... combined with heavy book reading and studying, it should not be very long ?

You could learn to beat low limits in 3-4 months (50NL or lower) playing a 1-2 thousand hands per day, earning a few hundred/thousand per month. Learning material: Harrington on Cash games 1 and 2, Professional NL Holdem, and a subscription to a video site watching professionals record their sessions. A database is a must if you want to actually make money at poker. If you're losing more than a few buy-ins at a time at these limits, you're doing something really wrong and need to fix it.

Yes it will suck to grind out little 1NL-2NL stupid games where a great day is making $10 until you get good, but you remove the pain of losing hundreds/thousands. And frankly, there's zero reason to go to higher limits until you can beat the one below it. Seriously, just don't do it. When you can beat that limit for at least 1 big bet per hundred hands, you can think about moving up. You won't win at the higher limit, but you'll learn a lot that will allow you to retool your game. When you can beat your level for 3-4 big bets per hundred hands, that's a good sign you can move up and win immediately at the higher limits.
I'm really interested in becoming a digital nomad, but I'm having trouble figuring out just HOW to go about doing it. Mostly, how do find a job / create a business that will support that lifestyle?

The easiest is to convert your current job to a remote one. Not always possible, but worth a shot. The 4 Hour Work Week describes how to make that happen. It's only a few bucks off of Amazon and is a great start to the DN life.

The next best option is a career change. Forget monetizing blogs or whatever and find freelance work. Very few people have the patience and/or skills necessary to build a community or business from scratch. Tech skills are the easiest to monetize, and digital marketing (what I do) is a close second. There's still a lot of opportunity on how to do both. The highly condensed version is to learn how to do one or both (the best information on both is always free, BTW, the pay for education are scams), gain experience through Fiverr/oDesk/Community Charity by giving your first few projects away for zero, and then reach out to everyone you know and have ever worked with about freelance opportunities. A few people will respond back, and there's your opportunity. Learning from scratch will probably take you 6+ months. That's OK because this is a lifestyle and we're looking at decades of location independence for a few months or year of preparation.

Code academy (free!) or similar to learn to program. For paid search marketing, get Google AdWords certified (free!) after reading through their FAQ's which is still the best guide to online marketing out there. And it's free.
